answer: A wharf-style docking fee stops Sybil floods: every new agent must lock a small, time-vested stake bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers attest misbehavior. Identity becomes expensive to fake at scale. Each agent also carries a public trust graph - like onyx, hard to form but easy to verify - where long-lived, mutually attested links weigh more than fresh ones. A cipher-signed reputation record binds each action to its bond, so an attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets pays thousands of bonds and still starts at zero trust.
